whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Consumer Goods Cloud Accredited Professional exam for?

personas.label: CPG implementation consultants
personas.description: You deliver Consumer Goods Cloud projects for CPG manufacturers and distributors and need the credential to validate your retail execution expertise.

personas.label: Salesforce admins in consumer goods
personas.description: You manage a Consumer Goods Cloud org and want to prove your knowledge of visit planning, in-store audits, and field team management.

personas.label: Retail execution and field sales partners
personas.description: You design solutions for field reps covering store visits, shelf compliance, and order capture and need to demonstrate your configuration skills.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Consumer Goods Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Consumer Goods Cloud AP exam is moderately difficult. It tests CPG-specific workflows like visit planning, in-store execution, direct store delivery, and retail analytics. Candidates without exposure to consumer goods field operations will find the domain terminology and retail execution concepts challenging.
bullets: ~65% passing score: roughly 39 correct answers needed.
Field execution workflows: you must understand visit plans, route optimisation, shelf audits, and how surveys capture compliance data during store visits.
Order and inventory management: questions cover direct store delivery (van sales), pricing rules, and inventory tracking at the vehicle level.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Score 75%+ on practice exams and ensure you understand the end-to-end retail execution workflow before booking. Hands-on experience with Consumer Goods Cloud visit planning or in-store audit configuration is strongly recommended.

examFormat.heading: Consumer Goods Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 40-50% of questions are scenario-based. Common patterns include configuring visit plans for a beverage distributor, setting up shelf audit surveys for planogram compliance, and designing order workflows for direct store delivery.
bestWayToPass: Master visit planning: Know how to configure visit plans, route optimisation rules, visit templates, and priority scoring for different store tiers.
Understand in-store execution: Study how surveys, shelf audits, photo capture, and Einstein Vision work together for planogram compliance tracking.
Learn order management: Know the direct store delivery workflow from cart creation through invoicing, including price books, promotions, and vehicle inventory management.
Study analytics and KPIs: Understand key retail execution metrics like on-shelf availability, visit completion rate, and how CRM Analytics dashboards aggregate field performance data.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Consumer Goods Cloud implementation, visit planning, retail execution, in-store audits, direct store delivery, and field team performance management for CPG companies. The exam is 33 scored questions in 60 minutes, with a 64% pass mark, weighted towards Data Setup and Visit Execution (36% each).

keyConcepts.h2: Consumer Goods Cloud AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Visit Planning & Route Optimization
blocks.body: Consumer Goods Cloud supports field sales and merchandising teams that visit retail stores. Visit Plans define which stores to visit, visit frequency, and visit activities. Route Optimization calculates the most efficient travel sequence for a sales rep's daily visits. Visit Templates specify which tasks (surveys, order taking, shelf audits) are required at each store type. Priority scoring ranks stores for visit scheduling based on sales volume or compliance risk. The AP exam tests how to configure visit plans, assign them to field teams, and set up route optimization rules. Know the difference between manual route assignment and automated optimization.

blocks.heading: In-Store Execution & Retail Audits
blocks.body: During a store visit, the field rep uses the Salesforce mobile app to complete Activities: shelf audits (planogram compliance), order capture, promotions execution, and competitive data collection. Surveys capture structured data, product availability, shelf position, facing count. Photos attached to visit records document compliance issues. Einstein Vision can analyze shelf images for planogram compliance. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) measure execution quality per store and rep. The exam tests how to configure survey questions, how photos are attached and surfaced in reports, and how to set up KPI targets for field team performance management.

blocks.heading: Order Management & Direct Store Delivery
blocks.body: Van Sales (Direct Store Delivery) orders are captured in the field and fulfilled from a delivery vehicle. The order workflow: create cart → confirm order → generate invoice → collect payment → update inventory. Price Books and Price Rules support store-specific and account-specific pricing. Promotions and trade deals apply discounts at the line item level. Inventory management tracks on-hand stock in the delivery vehicle. Returns are processed on-site with inventory adjustments. The exam tests the end-to-end DSD order flow, how pricing rules stack, and how inventory is tracked at the vehicle location level.

blocks.heading: Account & Store Management
blocks.body: Retail accounts (stores, chains, distributors) are managed as Account records with consumer goods-specific fields (store type, chain affiliation, territory). Store Clusters group similar accounts for targeted promotional strategies. Assortment Plans define which products should be available at each store or cluster. Planogram compliance measures whether the right products are shelved in the right positions. Account plans and joint business plans track collaborative goals with key retail partners. The exam tests how to configure assortment plans, how to link planograms to store accounts, and how to set up account plan templates for key account management.

blocks.heading: Analytics & Field Performance Reporting
blocks.body: Consumer Goods Cloud reports and dashboards measure field execution quality, sell-in vs. sell-out performance, and promotional effectiveness. Visit Completion Rate, OSA (On-Shelf Availability), and planogram compliance are key metrics. **Einstein Analytics** ([CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant)) apps for Consumer Goods provide pre-built dashboards for territory managers. Scorecards aggregate KPIs at the rep, territory, and national levels. Alerts notify managers when execution falls below threshold. The exam tests which standard reports are available, how to configure custom KPI scorecards, and how CRM Analytics datasets are populated from visit activity data.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Consumer Goods Cloud AP exam tests configuration of field execution solutions for CPG companies. Focus on visit planning, in-store execution, retail audits, and the Consumer Goods data model.

blocks.heading: Consumer Goods Data Model
blocks.body: Know the CG Cloud objects: Retail Store, Account (retailer), Product, Planogram, Assessment, and Visit. Understand how these objects relate and how the data model supports field rep execution.

blocks.heading: Visit Planning & Scheduling
blocks.body: Know how to configure visit plans: route planning, call cycle rules, visit frequency by store tier, and how the route management optimization engine assigns visits to reps efficiently.

blocks.heading: In-Store Execution & Audits
blocks.body: Know how to configure Assessment Tasks (shelf audits, compliance checks) within visits. Understand how tasks are assigned, how survey responses are captured, and how photos are attached via the mobile app.

blocks.heading: Einstein Vision for Shelf Recognition
blocks.body: Know how Einstein Vision (image recognition) is used in Consumer Goods Cloud for shelf compliance: training the model with planogram data, capturing shelf photos, and how compliance scores are calculated.

blocks.heading: Analytics & Reporting
blocks.body: Know the standard CG Cloud reports and dashboards: visit compliance rates, distribution KPIs, survey response trends, and how [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant) is used for advanced territory and account performance analysis.

nextCertsAfter.intro: AP credentials pair well with core platform certifications. Consider:

sampleQuestions.question: A field rep visits 20 stores a week and needs their call plan on a tablet with no signal in the back of shop. What supports this?
options: A web browser session kept open on the tablet for the whole of the working day
A printed route sheet produced each morning and typed up again that evening
The offline-capable mobile app
A nightly email containing the full list of stores the rep has to visit next
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retail execution happens in places with poor connectivity, so the app stores the visit, its tasks and the data captured, then syncs when a signal returns.
whyWrong: A browser session drops as soon as connectivity goes and loses unsaved work.
Paper means double entry and a day's delay before anyone sees the data.
An email list cannot capture what the rep records during the visit.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a retail store visit record in Consumer Goods Cloud represent?
options: The promotional discount agreed with the retailer for a particular period
The stock currently held in the distribution centre serving that outlet
The monthly invoice raised against the retailer for the goods delivered
A planned or completed call at an outlet
sampleQuestions.explanation: A visit is the unit of field work. It carries the date, the outlet, the rep and the tasks to be completed while they are there.
whyWrong: Promotions are commercial agreements, not field visits.
Warehouse stock is a supply chain record.
Invoicing is handled in order management and finance.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep must check shelf stock. Take a photo and place a reorder during one visit. How is this structured?
options: As three separate visits to the same outlet on the same day of the week
As three cases raised against the retailer's account for someone to action
As tasks on the visit
As a single free-text note the rep types up at the end of the whole visit
sampleQuestions.explanation: Visit tasks break the call into the specific actions required, which makes completion measurable and keeps the captured data structured.
whyWrong: Splitting one call into three visits distorts the visit metrics.
Cases are for issues to resolve, not planned field work.
Free text cannot be reported on or compared across outlets.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a planogram in retail execution?
options: It defines how products should be arranged on shelf
It lists every single product the retailer has ordered over the past year
It schedules the delivery vehicles serving the outlets in a given region
It records the payment terms that have been agreed with the retailer
sampleQuestions.explanation: A planogram is the agreed shelf layout, and comparing it against what the rep finds in store is how compliance is measured.
whyWrong: Order history is a transactional record, not a layout.
Delivery scheduling is a logistics function.
Payment terms are commercial, not merchandising.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep photographs a shelf and the system identifies which products are present. What is this called?
options: A manual stock count entered by the rep into the app during the visit
Image recognition for shelf audit
An order placed automatically against the distribution centre for that region
A planogram template downloaded from the retailer's own merchandising team
sampleQuestions.explanation: Image recognition reads the photo and reports what is on shelf, which is far faster and more consistent than counting by hand.
whyWrong: The point of image recognition is that it replaces the manual count.
Ordering is a separate step that may follow the audit.
A template describes the target layout rather than reading the actual shelf.

sampleQuestions.question: Why does a consumer goods company care about share of shelf?
options: Shelf space drives what shoppers actually buy
Retailers are required by regulation to report it publicly every quarter
It determines the payment terms the retailer is willing to offer the supplier
It sets the number of field reps the company is permitted to employ
sampleQuestions.explanation: Products that are visible and well placed sell more, so the proportion of shelf a brand holds is a direct commercial measure.
whyWrong: There is no such public reporting requirement.
Payment terms are negotiated separately from shelf position.
Field headcount is an internal resourcing decision.

sampleQuestions.question: A promotion runs for six weeks across 300 outlets. What is the useful measure of its success?
options: The number of promotional display units that were shipped to the retailers
The count of photographs the reps uploaded while the promotion was running
The total number of outlets the field team managed to visit during the period
Sales lift against a comparable baseline period
sampleQuestions.explanation: A promotion is judged by whether it moved more product than the equivalent period without it, which requires a baseline to compare against.
whyWrong: Units shipped measures logistics, not sales to shoppers.
Photo volume measures data capture, not performance.
Visit coverage measures field activity, not commercial outcome.

sampleQuestions.question: What does trade promotion management address?
options: Recruiting and scheduling the field representatives across each territory
Planning and funding promotions with retailers
Designing the packaging artwork used for each product in the range
Routing the delivery vehicles that serve each of the retail outlets daily
sampleQuestions.explanation: Trade promotion management covers the agreement, funding and measurement of promotions run with retail partners.
whyWrong: Field scheduling is workforce management.
Packaging design is a marketing and production activity.
Vehicle routing is transport planning.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep finds a product out of stock on shelf while the back room holds plenty. What is the issue?
options: An error in the planogram agreed with the retailer's merchandising team
A replenishment problem inside the store
A pricing dispute that has not yet been resolved with the retailer
A manufacturing shortage at the supplier's own production facility
sampleQuestions.explanation: Stock on site but not on shelf is a store execution issue, and flagging it is one of the most valuable things a visit produces.
whyWrong: The layout is not the cause when the shelf is simply unfilled.
Pricing does not explain why available stock is not displayed.
Supply is clearly fine, because the stock is in the building.

sampleQuestions.question: Why is visit frequency usually set differently for different outlets?
options: Field representatives are contractually limited to a fixed number of calls
Retailers insist that every one of their stores is visited on the same day
The mobile app can only synchronise a small number of visits each week
Outlets differ in size and sales potential
sampleQuestions.explanation: A large high-turnover store justifies more attention than a small one, so frequency is matched to the value of the outlet.
whyWrong: Contracts do not normally dictate call patterns per outlet.
Simultaneous visits across a chain are not operationally possible.
Sync capacity is not what limits a call plan.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the benefit of capturing competitor presence during a visit?
options: It shows how the category is really performing
It satisfies a retailer requirement to report on all brands in the store
It removes the need to measure the company's own share of shelf at all
It allows the company to set the competitor's prices in that retail outlet
sampleQuestions.explanation: Your own numbers mean little without the context of what else is on shelf and how the whole category is moving.
whyWrong: This is not a retailer reporting obligation.
Competitor data complements your own measures rather than replacing them.
A supplier cannot set a competitor's prices.

sampleQuestions.question: A field manager wants to know whether reps are completing their planned calls. What should they look at?
options: Visit completion against the call plan
The quantity of product shipped to the region during the same time period
The total number of photographs that have been uploaded across the territory
The number of promotions that were agreed with retailers over the quarter
sampleQuestions.explanation: Comparing completed visits with the plan is the direct measure of whether field activity is happening as intended.
whyWrong: Shipment volume reflects orders, not field discipline.
Photo volume is a by-product and can be high while calls are missed.
Promotion count measures commercial activity, not call execution.

sampleQuestions.question: What should happen to data captured offline once the device regains connectivity?
options: It is held on the device until an administrator approves the upload manually
It syncs to the org automatically
It is discarded; because only data captured while online can be trusted
It is emailed to the field manager as an attachment for them to key in
sampleQuestions.explanation: The whole point of offline capture is that the work survives the lack of signal and lands in the org once there is one.
whyWrong: Requiring manual approval for every sync would not scale to a field team.
Offline data is as valid as anything captured online.
Emailing data back for rekeying defeats the purpose of the app.

sampleQuestions.question: Why would a company audit price on shelf during a visit?
options: Suppliers are legally required to enforce the price the retailer displays
It is the only way to establish what the retailer has actually ordered
Retail price affects demand and brand positioning
It determines the commission the field representative will be paid
sampleQuestions.explanation: The shelf price shapes what shoppers buy and how the brand is perceived, so a supplier wants to know what it actually is.
whyWrong: A supplier generally cannot dictate a retailer's price.
Order quantities come from the order records.
Rep commission is not normally based on shelf price.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best describes what Consumer Goods Cloud is for?
options: Designing the range of products the company will launch in the coming year
Running the manufacturing schedule across each of the production facilities
Managing field execution at retail outlets
Handling the payroll and expenses for the field representatives employed
sampleQuestions.explanation: It supports the work of getting products properly stocked, priced and displayed in stores, through visit planning, execution and measurement.
whyWrong: Range planning is a product management activity.
Production scheduling is a manufacturing system's job.
Payroll and expenses are handled in human resources systems.
